title: Short-term rental communities, YouTube channels, books and newsletters worth your time
summary: The short-term rental communities, YouTube channels, books and newsletters worth following, with official links checked November 2026.
body_markdown:
**The best free education in short-term rentals is other hosts. Here's where to find them: the communities and forums worth joining, the YouTube channels worth watching, the books worth reading (including two that aren't about rentals at all), and the newsletters that keep you current. Every item links to its official page, checked November 19, 2026. Where we couldn't verify a member or subscriber count, we don't give one.**


## Key takeaways


- **Start with Airbnb's own Community Center** for platform questions, and one independent forum (Reddit or BiggerPockets) for honest answers.
- **YouTube:** Robuilt and BiggerPockets for investing, Thanks For Visiting for hosting, Optimize My Airbnb for listings.
- **Books:** *Short-Term Rental, Long-Term Wealth* for buying, *Get Paid For Your Pad* for hosting, and *Unreasonable Hospitality* and *Setting the Table* for the guest experience.
- **Newsletters:** VRM Intel and Rental Scale-Up for industry news, AirDNA for market data, ShortTermRentalz for the UK.
- **Treat group advice as a lead, not a rule.** Check anything about Airbnb policy against Airbnb's own help pages.

## Where we're coming from


We host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree, and before ProhostAI I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team. One thing I'd tell every new host: the fastest way to learn is from hosts a year or two ahead of you. The second thing: a confident answer in a Facebook group is not the same as Airbnb's policy, so always check the source. We make ProhostAI; nothing on this list is sponsored.


## Communities and forums


**Airbnb Community Center** (official). Boards for new hosts, optimizing your listing, hospitality, growing a hosting business, and a general café. Airbnb staff moderate, and it's the right place for questions about how a platform feature works.[communitycenter.airbnb.com](https://communitycenter.airbnb.com/)


**Airbnb Host Clubs** (official). Local, in-person and online groups of hosts organized through Airbnb. Good for market-specific questions like permits and cleaners.[Find a local club](https://www.airbnb.com/e/local-hosts-connect)


**r/airbnb_hosts** on Reddit. Large, candid and host-only in spirit. Good for "has anyone else seen this?" questions.[reddit.com/r/airbnb_hosts](https://www.reddit.com/r/airbnb_hosts/)


**BiggerPockets Forums,** short-term and vacation rental board. Investor-heavy, good for financing, markets and the numbers behind a purchase.[biggerpockets.com/forums](https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums)


**Facebook groups.** The big ones are "Professional Hosts," "Superhost Tips and Tricks" and "Short Term Rental University." They're very active. Search the group before you post; most questions have been answered many times.


### How to get good answers in a host group


- **Search first.** Most questions in big groups have been answered many times.
- **Give the context:** your market, your number of units, the platform, and what you've already tried. "Guest wants a refund" gets guesses. "Airbnb, two-night stay, hot tub broke on night one, guest asked for 50% back" gets useful answers.
- **Ask for sources on policy.** If someone says "Airbnb will remove that review," ask which part of the[Reviews Policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) they mean.
- **Weight answers from hosts like you.** Advice from a 200-unit manager and from a one-cabin host can both be right for different businesses.
- **Never post guest details.** Names, screenshots of messages with personal information, or addresses don't belong in a public group.


## YouTube channels


**Robuilt** (Rob Abasolo). Short-term rental investing, design and building, from a former BiggerPockets co-host.[youtube.com/@Robuilt](https://www.youtube.com/@Robuilt)


**BiggerPockets.** Real estate investing across strategies, with regular short-term rental episodes.[youtube.com/@biggerpockets](https://www.youtube.com/@biggerpockets)


**Thanks For Visiting.** The video side of the podcast: hosting, hospitality and guest experience for small hosts.[youtube.com/@ThanksForVisiting](https://www.youtube.com/@ThanksForVisiting)


**Optimize My Airbnb** (Danny Rusteen). Listing optimization: photos, titles, descriptions and pricing.[youtube.com/@OptimizeMyAirbnb](https://www.youtube.com/@OptimizeMyAirbnb)


**Michael Chang.** Short-term rental investing and operations.[youtube.com/@michaelchangbnb](https://www.youtube.com/@michaelchangbnb)


**Kylee and Steven.** Building and running a short-term rental business as a couple.[youtube.com/@kyleeandsteven](https://www.youtube.com/@kyleeandsteven)


**Airbnb Automated** (Sean Rakidzich). Automation and systems for running rentals at scale.[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCvwmrPfn8ff-rTlc9YoH7Bg)


### What to watch for on YouTube


Channels are made to be watched, so the most dramatic numbers get the thumbnails. When a video says a property makes a certain amount, look for what's behind it: gross or net, before or after cleaning and fees, one great year or several. Use our free[Airbnb profit calculator](https://prohost.ai/tools/airbnb-profit-calculator) to run the numbers for a property you're considering instead of taking a thumbnail's word for it.


## Books


**About short-term rentals**


- ***Short-Term Rental, Long-Term Wealth*** by Avery Carl (BiggerPockets Publishing, 2021). How to find, finance and buy a short-term rental, from the host of The Short Term Show.
- ***Get Paid For Your Pad*** by Jasper Ribbers and Huzefa Kapadia (2014). An early hosting playbook from the host of the podcast of the same name. Some platform details have changed; the hosting principles haven't.
- ***The Airbnb Story*** by Leigh Gallagher (Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, 2017). How Airbnb started and grew. Useful context on why the platform works the way it does.


**About hospitality (not rentals, but just as useful)**


- ***Unreasonable Hospitality*** by Will Guidara (Optimism Press, 2022). The former co-owner of Eleven Madison Park on going beyond service to hospitality. Read it before you design your welcome.
- ***Setting the Table*** by Danny Meyer (HarperCollins, 2006). The restaurateur behind Union Square Hospitality Group on putting the guest experience at the center of a business.


## Newsletters and news


- **VRM Intel.** Industry news for professional property managers, plus a quarterly magazine.[vrmintel.com](https://www.vrmintel.com/)
- **Rental Scale-Up.** Free weekly newsletter with news and analysis for managers.[rentalscaleup.com/newsletter](https://www.rentalscaleup.com/newsletter)
- **AirDNA.** Monthly newsletter and a Monthly Market Review of supply, demand and rates.[airdna.co](https://www.airdna.co/monthly-market-review)
- **Skift.** Travel industry news, with a short-term rental section.[skift.com/vacation-rentals](https://skift.com/vacation-rentals/)
- **ShortTermRentalz.** UK and European short-term rental trade news with a weekly newsletter.[shorttermrentalz.com](https://shorttermrentalz.com/)


Two notes on keeping up. First, pick one news source and one data source, not five; most stories appear in all of them within a week. Second, read anything about regulation in your own market at the source. A newsletter will tell you a county is considering a cap. Only the county's own page tells you what was actually passed and when it takes effect, which is what we relied on for our[Hawaii taxes and county rules guide](https://prohost.ai/blog/hawaii-short-term-rental-taxes-and-county-rules) .


For podcasts, see our separate list of[the best short-term rental podcasts](https://prohost.ai/blog/best-short-term-rental-podcasts) , and for events,[short-term rental conferences in 2027](https://prohost.ai/blog/short-term-rental-conferences-2027) .


## Where to start, by situation


- **Thinking about your first property:** BiggerPockets Forums, Robuilt or BiggerPockets on YouTube, and *Short-Term Rental, Long-Term Wealth* .
- **Hosting your first one to three units:** Airbnb's Community Center, your local Host Club, the Thanks For Visiting channel, and our[first-time host guide](https://prohost.ai/blog/first-time-short-term-rental-host-guide) .
- **Growing past five units:** r/airbnb_hosts for operations questions, Airbnb Automated for systems, and the Rental Scale-Up newsletter.
- **Running a management company:** VRM Intel, Rental Scale-Up and AirDNA's market review, plus the in-person events in our[2027 conference list](https://prohost.ai/blog/short-term-rental-conferences-2027) .
- **Improving the guest experience at any size:** *Unreasonable Hospitality* and *Setting the Table* .


## Official sources worth bookmarking


Communities and creators are great for ideas. For rules, go to the source:


- **Airbnb Help Center** for policy:[how search results work](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/39) ,[response rate](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/430) ,[Superhost](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/829) ,[reviews](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) and[host cancellations](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/990) .
- **Airbnb Resource Center** for Airbnb's own hosting guides:[airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes) .
- **Your city and county** for permits and taxes. Our guides to[Hawaii](https://prohost.ai/blog/hawaii-short-term-rental-guide) ,[the Smokies](https://prohost.ai/blog/smoky-mountains-cabin-rental-guide) and[Joshua Tree](https://prohost.ai/blog/joshua-tree-short-term-rental-guide) show what to look for.


We also wrote up[what I learned on Airbnb's hosting team](https://prohost.ai/blog/what-i-learned-on-airbnbs-hosting-team) , using only Airbnb's public pages.


## A learning plan you can copy


```text
STR LEARNING PLAN (one quarter)


Join (1):        Airbnb Community Center / a Host Club / r/airbnb_hosts / BiggerPockets
Watch (1):       ______________________  (1 video a week)
Read (1):        ______________________  (1 chapter a week)
Subscribe (1):   ______________________


Every week, write one line:
What I learned:          ______________________
What I changed:          ______________________
Did it help? (reviews, bookings, time saved): ______


Rule: before acting on advice about Airbnb policy,
check it on airbnb.com/help.


```


## Keep it running


Learning takes time, and most hosts don't have spare time until routine work comes off their plate.[AI messaging](https://prohost.ai/messaging) handles the guest questions you'd otherwise answer by hand,[cleanings](https://prohost.ai/features/cleanings) are scheduled from checkouts, and[AI reviews](https://prohost.ai/features/reviews) are written on time. What stays with you is what you learn from all of the above and decide to change.


## FAQ


**What's the best online community for Airbnb hosts?** For platform questions, Airbnb's Community Center. For candid peer advice, r/airbnb_hosts or the BiggerPockets forums.


**What's the best book on short-term rentals?** For buying, *Short-Term Rental, Long-Term Wealth* . For hospitality, *Unreasonable Hospitality* .


**Are Facebook host groups worth it?** Yes, for ideas and local contacts. Check policy claims against Airbnb's own help pages.


**Which newsletter should a property manager read?** VRM Intel and Rental Scale-Up for news, AirDNA for market data.


**Is there a free way to learn hosting?** All the communities, channels and newsletters above are free. So is Airbnb's[Resource Center](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes) .


**How do I find hosts in my own market?** Start with an[Airbnb Host Club](https://www.airbnb.com/e/local-hosts-connect) near you, then search Facebook for your town or county name plus "hosts" or "vacation rental owners." Local groups are where you'll find cleaners, handymen and permit advice for your exact area.


## The takeaway


Join one community, watch one channel, read one book and subscribe to one newsletter. Write down one thing you change each week. Check every policy claim at the source. A quarter of that will teach you more than a year of reading everything.
